Class C fire extinguishers are specifically designed for fires involving energized electrical equipment. These extinguishers use non-conductive extinguishing agents that won't conduct electricity back to the user.

The classes of fire extinguishers correspond to different types of fires:
- Class A: Ordinary combustibles (wood, paper, cloth, plastics, etc.)
- Class B: Flammable liquids and gases
- Class C: Electrical equipment/fires
- Class D: Combustible metals
- Class K: Cooking oils and fats
